subtopic: Constant folding / CSE / DCE / IR rewrite
learningObjective: Given a small IR fragment, identify which classical optimization (constant folding, CSE, DCE) is applied and confirm semantic preservation.
irSnippet:
// Before
%c1 = const 2
%c2 = const 3
%t1 = mul %c1, %c2       // = 6
%t2 = mul %c1, %c2       // = 6
%t3 = add %x, %t1
%t4 = add %x, %t2
%unused = mul %x, %x     // never used later
return %t3, %t4

// After
%c6  = const 6
%tsum = add %x, %c6
return %tsum, %tsum
stem: Which sequence of classical optimizations transforms the 'Before' IR into the 'After' IR, and is the rewrite semantics-preserving?

options.text: Only constant folding is applied; the duplicate `add %x, %c6` values are not detected because CSE cannot fold across use points, and `%unused` is retained since DCE would violate side-effect ordering.

Constant folding fuses `%t1 = mul 2, 3` into `%c6 = const 6`; CSE identifies `%t3` and `%t4` as syntactically equivalent `add %x, %c6` and collapses them to one value; DCE removes `%unused`. All three preserve semantics.
The rewrite is illegal: returning `%tsum` twice from a function violates SSA form because a single value cannot flow to two return slots.
Loop-invariant code motion is applied to hoist `mul %c1, %c2` out of the loop; CSE and DCE are unrelated to this particular rewrite.

explanation: Option B is correct; options A, C, D are incorrect. A (Wrong): mischaracterizes the reach of CSE and DCE. B (Correct): constant folding + CSE + DCE composition; all semantics-preserving. C (Wrong): SSA allows a value to have many uses. D (Wrong): no loop is present; LICM is irrelevant to this fragment. General context: The 'Before → After' rewrite is a canonical composition of three classical optimizations: constant folding (evaluate `mul 2, 3` at compile time), CSE (recognize `%t3` and `%t4` compute the same expression on the same operands, so they are one value), and DCE (remove `%unused` since it has no consumer and no side effect). All three are semantics-preserving on pure operations. Option D introduces an irrelevant loop context.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: mischaracterizes the reach of CSE and DCE.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: constant folding + CSE + DCE composition; all semantics-preserving.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: SSA allows a value to have many uses.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: no loop is present; LICM is irrelevant to this fragment.

assumptions: `mul` and `add` are pure operations without side effects.
The return signature is a tuple that can hold two references to the same SSA value.
nonImplications: Does not imply CSE can always eliminate `add %x, %c6` duplicates across function boundaries — it operates within a scope defined by the pass.
Does not imply DCE can always remove any unused op — ops with observable side effects are exempt.

distractorRationales.A: Underestimates CSE/DCE reach on pure ops.
